clusters.name: Walter's move across the country, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter moving the family from Millbrook to Sorrel Valley in March 1952 and buying an apple orchard: June homesick and writing daily to her sister Edna, Walter out in the trees from dark to dark, Glen in fights at his new school, Walter cutting off his brother Harlan over their father's land money, June kept to her bed for weeks that winter, Walter and June in rows over money for new trees. By September 1953, June joined the church choir and her letters to Edna thinned out; her anxiety dropped and her functioning rose, and the period settles there.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard failing in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter drinking heavily most nights, Walter and Glen blaming each other, Glen and Marian taking over the family's money and talks with the bank, Carl's asthma attacks worse that winter, you wetting the bed again, your grandmother Ida's heart trouble found. By October 1969, Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees; his functioning rose and the period settles there.

clusters.name: Glen losing his job at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: Glen sat in the truck in the yard for hours out of work most of that year, he and Marian in loud fights at night over money, Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night, you stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer, you kept to your room and said little to your mother, your grandfather Walter drinking again after six years off it. By June 1976, you were eating again and made the track team; your functioning rose and the period settles there.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into your house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma, your partner's mother, selling her farm and moving into your house in January 1990: you clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals, you worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows while Hollis took his mother's side, Owen had tantrums at preschool, Wilma took over Lily's care, you broke out in eczema on both hands, you and Hollis in rows most nights. By June 1991, Wilma took a flat in town; in August your eczema cleared over the summer and your symptom dropped, and the period settles there.
